newsitem.title: USA: Calif. cities sponsor bills to reform tax measure.
newsitem.headline: Calif. cities sponsor bills to reform tax measure.

text.p: The League of California Cities on Friday introduced legislation to help cities implement Proposition 218, a controversial tax reform measure approved last November by the state's voters.

The League said the legislation, contained in two bills, would address the "inconsistent and contradictory provisions of Proposition 218," which requires voter approval of an array of taxes, assessments and fees levied by local governments.

"The League-sponsored legislation is written to help cities make Proposition 218 work in communities, not to circumvent or stop Proposition 218," said League President Ron Bates. "Cities need this legislation to work out the rough areas of Proposition 218."

The League's Senate bill, by Republican state Senator Richard Rainey, sets out the process for local governments to present tax measures for voter approval, as well as the time period to challenge the validity of taxes.
The Senate bill was introduced as an urgency measure requiring a two-thirds vote of the state legislature.

The League said its other bill, authored by Assemblywoman Deborah Ortiz, a Democrat, would address the longer-term issues created by Proposition 218 and could provide cities with more fiscal certainty.
Hearings on the proposed legislation were expected to begin in late March.
The League of California Cities represents California's 471 cities in the state legislature.
